source: Direct MUSITU Axiom connected operation calls, four actual executions
inputs: Synthetic illustrative data only; no customer or live market data

cases.title: Evaluate an investment with NPV
cases.question: Does a four-year project create value at a 10% discount rate?
cases.interpretation: The hypothetical discounted inflows exceed the 100,000-unit starting investment by approximately 11,215.08 units.
cases.method: Net present value discounts each period's cash flow by (1 + rate) raised to that period.
cases.verification: Axiom independent decimal-discount recurrence verified; residual 2.08e-11
cases.prompt: Using MUSITU Axiom finance.npv, calculate the NPV of cash flows [-100000, 30000, 40000, 45000, 25000] at a discount rate of 0.10. Show the result and assumptions.

cases.title: Understand historical portfolio risk
cases.question: What does the 95% historical value-at-risk estimate say about example periodic returns?
cases.interpretation: The example estimates a 3.245% historical loss threshold at the chosen confidence level. Twenty synthetic observations are too few to establish a reliable forward-looking risk estimate.
cases.method: Historical VaR uses the empirical tail of observed return losses at a chosen confidence level.
cases.verification: Executed with MUSITU Axiom; no independent-verification flag returned
cases.prompt: Using MUSITU Axiom finance.var_historical, estimate 95% VaR for these 20 synthetic returns: [0.012,-0.018,0.009,-0.025,0.015,-0.041,0.022,-0.012,0.017,-0.032,0.006,-0.008,0.019,-0.022,0.010,-0.015,0.013,-0.028,0.004,-0.011]. Interpret the result cautiously.

cases.title: Find a relationship with linear regression
cases.question: How do example outcomes move as a predictor increases?
cases.interpretation: For these eight synthetic pairs, the fitted outcome increases by about 2.008 units per predictor unit; association alone does not establish causation.
cases.method: Least-squares linear regression fits an intercept and slope to paired observations.
cases.verification: Executed with MUSITU Axiom; no independent-verification flag returned
cases.prompt: Using MUSITU Axiom statistics.regression, fit x=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] and y=[3.1,4.8,7.2,8.9,11.1,12.8,15.0,17.2]. Report slope, intercept and interpretation.

cases.title: Make a constrained allocation decision
cases.question: How should two activities be allocated to maximise a simple score under three limits?
cases.summary: Optimal allocation: x = 2, y = 2; maximum score = 10
cases.interpretation: With x + y ≤ 4, x ≤ 2 and y ≤ 3, the maximum of 3x + 2y is 10 at (2,2). Axiom minimised the equivalent negative objective.
cases.method: Linear programming searches feasible allocations against linear limits and an objective.
cases.verification: Axiom rational primal–dual verification: feasible with exact zero duality gap
cases.prompt: Using MUSITU Axiom optimization.linear_program, maximise 3x+2y subject to x+y<=4, x<=2, y<=3 and x,y>=0. Translate to the minimisation input c=[-3,-2] and explain the optimal allocation.
